behavior: A part that keeps nodes beside its element has one root node: a trigger with focus guards, and `Toast.Viewport` with its focus guard and its alert region. A popup part with a focus manager also has one root node, with its two inside focus guards beside its element. `Combobox.Input` and `Combobox.Popup` also have one root node, with their dismiss button beside their element. `Select.Popup` has one root node, because `Select.Positioner` holds its style element. A part that renders its element only in some states has one root node too. `Collapsible.Panel`, `Dialog.Backdrop` and `Tabs.Indicator` are examples. The root is its element, or one comment while it has no element. A rule of `<style scoped>`, `v-show`, a custom directive and `<Transition>` of the consumer thus apply to the element of the part, also while the nodes are in the document. The script of `Tabs.Indicator` with `renderBeforeHydration` is the last child of its element. A portal part has one root node too, its `Teleport`, also while the portal keeps its focus guards and its owner element beside it. With Vue 3.5.41 or later, a `<Transition>` of the consumer thus applies to the portal element of a part with no `#render` slot. In Vue 3.6, it applies from 3.6.0-rc.3. `NavigationMenu.Content` has a `<Teleport>` as its root, so a scoped rule, `v-show`, a directive and a `<Transition>` of the developer do not reach its default element. The `element` slot and the prop `transition` give them.
